summary: Youngest child of the Irish Quaker immigrant William Albertson and Hannah Drewett, born c. 1706 (the tree's 1692 is a land deed mutated into a birthdate). Orphaned of his father at about three, he grew into the Otter Branch tract left him by the 1709 will, worked it as a shoemaker-farmer, married Ann Austin of Evesham under Newton (Haddonfield) Meeting in late 1727, built the brick Albertson homestead in 1743 that gave its name to the modern Albertson locality, raised eight daughters and a son, outlived that son, and died on his plantation in the winter of 1783/84, aged about 78, leaving the farm to his grandson John.

place.raw: Gloucester County, West New Jersey (possibly Byberry, Pennsylvania)

waypoints.narrative: Born around 1706, youngest of William and Hannah's three children. The '1692' of family lore is impossible — Hannah was married to William Stockdale until 1693 — and traces to his father's 1692 Gloucester land purchase. The family seat at the time was actually Byberry on the Poquessing, so his birthplace may be Pennsylvania rather than the Gloucester of the compiled trees.

place.raw: Otter Branch, Gloucester Township, Gloucester County, New Jersey

waypoints.narrative: His father died when Josiah was about three; the will of 7 December 1709 set aside for him the Gloucester Township tract bounded by Otter Branch of Timber Creek — the land that would anchor the rest of his life.

place.raw: Newton (later Haddonfield) Monthly Meeting, New Jersey

waypoints.narrative: Declared intentions with Ann Austin, daughter of Francis Austin of Evesham, at the meeting in September 1727; Friends custom put the marriage about two to three months later, which makes the tree's 12 November 1727 entirely credible as the wedding itself. They would raise nine children under the care of Haddonfield Meeting.

place.raw: Otter Branch homestead (modern Magnolia/Albertson, New Jersey)

waypoints.narrative: A shoemaker as well as farmer and lumberman, he doubled his acreage and in 1743 built the brick Albertson homestead, which stood into the late nineteenth century — the family name survives on the map in the Albertson locality near Magnolia.

The '9 Mar 1768, Burlington' entry in the export is Ancestry's mislabeled Haddonfield MM material — plausibly the meeting's proceedings around son Josiah Jr.'s marriage to Eleanor Tomlinson. He and Ann also appear witnessing a Haddonfield marriage certificate back in 1741.

place.raw: Otter Branch plantation, Gloucester Township, Gloucester County, New Jersey

waypoints.narrative: Made his will 7 December 1783 — 'Josiah Albertson, of Gloucester Township, yeoman' — leaving the plantation to grandson John, his only son Josiah Jr. having died the previous winter. The estate inventory of £130.14.3 was taken 10 March 1784 and the will proved on the 16th: the date family trees mistook for his death. He was about 78, not the 92 the false 1692 birth implied.

notes: Reviewed 2026-07-03 against Calendar of NJ Wills VI pp. 11-12 (will, inventory, probate), Clement (1877), Prowell (1886), Craig's South Jersey Marriages (Haddonfield minutes), WikiTree Albertson-649. Death corrected from '16 Mar 1784 Haddonfield' to Dec 1783-Mar 1784 on the Gloucester Township plantation; probate date had been mistaken for death date.
